official.deadline_central_display: November 6, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. ET - deadline to submit the complete application
official.deadline_note: Earlier gates matter more: the eligibility screening form is due October 2, 2026; mandatory information sessions run in the weeks of October 5 and October 12, 2026; and all three references must be received by October 30, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. ET. The application period itself runs from September 1 to November 6, 2026.
official.status_note: The Foundation's 2027 application pages state that applications for the 2027 Scholarship are open to doctoral students in the first or second year of their PhD programme, with the two-step process live via the SmartSimple portal.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Up to $50,000 per year for three years - to cover tuition and living expenses related to your doctoral studies.
benefits: Up to $50,000 per year for three years, to cover tuition and living expenses related to doctoral studies
Up to $20,000 per year for research and travel, supporting research, networking activities, and travel related to the doctoral work
Mentorship and experiential learning: meetings, masterclasses, seminars and field experiences with Mentors, Fellows and Scholars
Membership in an engaged multidisciplinary community of Scholars, Fellows and Mentors
A network of more than 500 Foundation alumni
eligibility: At the time of application, be in the first year or the second year of a PhD programme
Field of study broadly related to the humanities or social sciences and addressing issues relevant to Canada's future
PhD research aligned with at least one of the Foundation's four themes: Human Rights and Dignity; Responsible Citizenship; Canada and the World; People and their Natural Environment

Be a Canadian student enrolled at a Canadian university; a Canadian student enrolled at a university outside Canada; or an international student enrolled at a Canadian university. International students residing outside Canada or enrolled outside Canada are not eligible.
Demonstrate outstanding academic achievement and a high level of intellectual ability, assessed across the whole application including transcripts and letters of recommendation
Provide exactly three letters of reference: one from the PhD supervisor, one from another academic referee, and one from a referee outside academia
There is no age limit to apply
requirements: Complete the eligibility screening form first - only applicants whose eligibility is confirmed gain access to the full application form
Applications that do not meet the eligibility criteria will not be reviewed

Provide exactly three letters of reference (PhD supervisor, another academic referee, and a referee outside academia) - no more and no fewer, attached within the application file; they cannot be sent directly to the Foundation
The application form must be filled out in one language only, either English or French
Attend a mandatory information session in the week of October 5 or October 12, 2026
Declare all additional sources of income each year, including other scholarships
documents: Completed eligibility verification form on the SmartSimple portal
Completed full application form on the SmartSimple portal
Three letters of reference: one from the PhD supervisor, one from another academic referee, and one from a referee outside academia
Special Circumstances section explanation where a former supervisor or another professor must act as PhD supervisor referee
selection_criteria: Academic excellence, supported by an outstanding academic record
A compelling research project addressing issues shaping Canada's future, with clear alignment to the Foundation's mission and four founding themes
The rigour of the research proposal
The ability to share knowledge for the benefit of society, and willingness to engage in dialogue, interdisciplinary collaboration and knowledge sharing

Applicants who pass review are invited to group meetings and individual interviews conducted in French or English per the applicant's preference; final decisions are approved by the Board of Directors
coverage: Up to $50,000 per year for three years to cover tuition and living expenses related to doctoral studies
Up to $20,000 per year for research and travel, supporting research, networking activities, and travel related to the doctoral work
Mentorship, experiential learning and the Foundation's multidisciplinary community and alumni network
application_method: Read the published eligibility criteria and confirm your profile meets all requirements
Complete the short eligibility screening form on the SmartSimple portal (https://fdnpetf.smartsimple.ca) by October 2, 2026
Wait for the Foundation to confirm eligibility and grant access to the full application form
Attend a mandatory information session in the week of October 5 or October 12, 2026
Complete the full application form, including the research proposal and the Special Circumstances section where relevant
Nominate three referees within the application file so they receive the letter instructions; referees must submit their letters by October 30, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. ET
Submit the complete application by November 6, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. ET
official.application_route: Two-step SmartSimple process: eligibility screening form first (October 2), then the full application with three in-file reference letters, submitted by November 6, 2026.
official.study_mode: Full-time doctoral study (first or second year of the PhD programme at application)
official.citizenship_residency: Canadian students at Canadian or non-Canadian universities, or international students enrolled at a Canadian university; international students residing outside Canada or enrolled outside Canada are not eligible
official.international_eligibility: Yes - international students enrolled at a Canadian university are eligible; international students studying outside Canada are not
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Humanities or social sciences research aligned with at least one of the four founding themes (Human Rights and Dignity; Responsible Citizenship; Canada and the World; People and their Natural Environment), addressing issues relevant to Canada's future
official.research_requirement: A doctoral research project whose rigour and theme alignment are assessed; the research proposal is part of the application and shortlisted candidates are interviewed
official.description: The Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation PhD Scholarship supports doctoral students with an excellent academic record who are engaged in humanities and social sciences research that contributes to the advancement of Canada and society. Scholars receive up to $50,000 per year for three years to cover tuition and living expenses, plus up to $20,000 per year for research and travel, alongside mentorship and a community of more than 500 alumni.
official.english_requirement: Applicants must be able to communicate effectively in either French or English; the application form must be completed in one language only (English or French), and referees may respond in either language regardless of the language of the application. There is no requirement to be fluent in both official languages.

not_confirmed: exact stipend each Scholar receives (the published figure is 'up to $50,000 per year'; the actual award depends on the assessment, and additional income is declared annually)

verification.notes: Two official trudeaufoundation.ca pages were fetched in full. The scholarship page was verified for the benefit wording ('Up to $50,000 per year for three years - to cover tuition and living expenses'; 'Up to $20,000 per year for research and travel'), the four-theme alignment requirement, the three-letter reference structure and the selection criteria. The 2027 applications page was verified for the two-step process and all key dates (eligibility form October 2, 2026; information sessions weeks of October 5 and 12; references October 30, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. ET; application deadline November 6, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. ET).

applicant_utility.summary: The sequence is unforgiving: you must clear the eligibility screening form by October 2, 2026 just to unlock the full application, attend a mandatory information session, and get all three referees - supervisor, academic and one from outside academia - to submit by October 30 at 9:00 a.m. ET, five days before the November 6 deadline. Theme fit is a structural filter, not a bonus: your humanities or social sciences research must map onto one of the four founding themes, and you must be in year one or two of the PhD at application. Note the funding structure - the stipend is 'up to' $50,000 and is adjusted against other income you declare, though every Scholar keeps the full $20,000 research and travel allowance.
applicant_utility.best_fit: First- or second-year humanities and social sciences PhD students in Canada (or Canadians abroad) with an outstanding record whose research speaks to one of the four themes and who want mentorship and a cross-sector network as much as money.
application_readiness_checklist: Submit the eligibility screening form on SmartSimple by October 2, 2026 - the full form stays locked until eligibility is confirmed
Attend one of the mandatory information sessions in the weeks of October 5 or October 12, 2026
Identify your three referees early - supervisor, a second academic, and one outside academia - and give them the October 30, 9:00 a.m. ET deadline
Map your research explicitly onto at least one of the four founding themes in the proposal
Complete the form in one language only (English or French), and use the Special Circumstances section if your supervisor referee situation is unusual
Submit by November 6, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. ET and keep the confirmation email - the form disappears from the portal once the competition ends
common_rejection_risks: Missing the October 2 eligibility gate or the October 30 reference deadline - references cannot be sent directly to the Foundation outside the application file
Submitting two or four reference letters instead of exactly three
A research project that cannot be aligned to any of the four founding themes, or that sits outside humanities/social sciences
Being beyond the second year of the PhD at application
Applying as an international student enrolled outside Canada, which is excluded
Mixing languages in the application form
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The scholarship provides up to $50,000 per year toward tuition and living expenses plus up to $20,000 for research and travel; because the stipend is capped and adjusted against other declared income, students in high-tuition programmes may still carry costs, and relocation to a Canadian university is not separately funded.
document_audit: Reference letters must be uploaded inside the application file - the Foundation will not accept letters sent directly, and exactly three are required
The eligibility screening form is a gate, not a formality: applications failing the eligibility criteria are not reviewed at all
The Special Circumstances section is the only sanctioned route if a former supervisor or another professor must act as the supervisor referee
Once the competition closes the application form is removed from the portal - the confirmation email is your only proof of submission
alerts: The stipend value is adjusted against other awards and all additional income must be declared annually, but the full $20,000 research/travel allowance and a minimum stipend component are preserved regardless
Scholars may suspend the scholarship for up to one year for parental, medical, personal or professional leave, with payments paused until full-time re-enrolment
There is no return-home requirement for Canadian students studying abroad or for international students
Funds begin only after Board approval, signature of the funding agreement and submission of required documentation - do not rely on the award for first-month cash flow
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: SmartSimple eligibility form (October 2), mandatory information session, full application with in-file references by October 30, final submission by November 6, then group meetings and interviews for shortlisted candidates in French or English, with Board of Directors approval of final decisions.
